To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the consumption of RS by cats results in changes to the gut microbiota that are beneficial and that these changes are associated with increased production of immunoglobulin A.
dietary resistant starch (RS), a nondigestible starch, was incorporated into a commercial pet food and fed to cats.
dietary resistant starch (RS), preserved through mild extrudation of grain, alters fecal microbiota metabolism of dietary macromutrients, while increasing immunoglobulins A in the cat.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new class of functional food ingredients, dietary RS, and the demonstration that RS can provide health benefits to the cat host via microbiome mediated metabolism.
the effect that a dietary component, resistant starch, has on a cat's gut.
the effect of resistant starch on the gut health of cats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the feline microbiome responds to dietary resistant starch in a manner similar to that of the human microbiome.
the consumption of HRS food by cats produced beneficial changes in fecal metabolites and microbiota and elevated fecal IgA.

cats fed HRS food showed significantly greater concentrations of fecal immunoglobulins and metabolites associated to improved gut health and microbiota mediated metabolism of dietary macromolecules, while fecal metabolites associated to inflammation and oxidative stress were reduced.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cats consuming HRS foods had a fecal metabolome that more closely resembled that of dogs, a species that has a well documented beneficial RS response.

cats fed a grain based diet with a high RS content (HRS) have a fecal microbiome that metabolizes dietary macronutrient components differently than cats fed the low RS (LRS) food, resulting in greater fecal concentrations of the short chain fatty acid butyrate and a greater ratio of straight chain:braned chain fatty acids, and lower ammonia.
RS is a beneficial prebiotic that increases IgA and beneficial microbiome metabolite production in cats.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cat is capable of consuming a diet containing a significant amount of RS and that this diet is well tolerated.
cats are able to respond to the consumption of RS, and that this may be beneficial for the host.
RS is a promising ingredient for cat foods that may provide a means to enhance gut health and immune status.
